title: Kingdom of Commagene
capsule: The Kingdom of Commagene was a small Hellenistic-Iranian dynastic state positioned on the upper Euphrates around its capital Samosata (modern Samsat, Turkey), founded when the satrap Ptolemaeus declared autonomy from the Seleucids around 163 BC. Under Antiochus I Theos (c. 70–38 BC) the kingdom reached its cultural apogee, commissioning the extraordinary dynastic sanctuary atop Mount Nemrut — now a UNESCO World Heritage Site — where colossal statues of the king alongside Greek and Iranian deities proclaimed its syncretic identity. Rome annexed Commagene under Tiberius in 17 CE, restored it under Caligula in 38 CE, and definitively suppressed it under Vespasian in 72 CE when Legio VI Ferrata marched on Samosata, Antiochus IV surrendered, and the territory was incorporated into the province of Syria.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territory around Samosata is well defined through Strabo, Pliny, Josephus, and numismatic evidence; peripheral boundaries shifted with Roman reorganizations and are imprecisely mapped.
